record.paper_title: Billiard Dynamics: A Survey with the Emphasis on Open Problems
record.original_question: Let Y be a smooth, strictly convex planar billiard table, let Φ be the phase space of its billiard map, let 𝒫⊂Φ be the set of all periodic points, and let 𝒫_n⊂Φ be the set of periodic points of period n. With respect to the invariant Liouville measure μ on Φ, is μ(𝒫)=0? Equivalently, is μ(𝒫_n)=0 for every n?

evidence.quote: Let P ⊂ Φ (resp. Pn ⊂ Φ) be the set of periodic points (resp. periodic points of period n).
Problem 3. Let Y be any Birkhoff billiard table. i) Prove that µ(P) = 0. ii) Prove that µ(Pn) = 0 for all n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Y \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth, strictly convex planar domain, and consider the billiard map associated with $Y$: a point $x$ on the boundary $\partial Y$ together with an inward unit vector $v$ (making an angle in $(0,\pi)$ with the tangent to $\partial Y$ at $x$) is mapped to the next point of reflection on $\partial Y$ and the corresponding reflected unit vector. Let $\Phi$ denote the phase space of this map (parametrized, for instance, by arc length on $\partial Y$ and the angle of incidence), and let $\mu$ be the invariant Liouville measure on $\Phi$ (proportional to $\sin\varphi \, ds\, d\varphi$ in these coordinates). Let $\mathcal{P} \subset \Phi$ be the set of all periodic points of the billiard map, and for each integer $n \geq 2$ let $\mathcal{P}_n \subset \Phi$ be the set of points of period $n$.

(i) Prove that $\mu(\mathcal{P}) = 0$.

(ii) Prove that $\mu(\mathcal{P}_n) = 0$ for every $n \geq 2$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is Ivrii's conjecture (1980), which remains open in general. Partial results are known: the set of period-3 (triangular) orbits has measure zero, and for piecewise $C^4$ planar boundaries the set of period-4 (quadrilateral) orbits has measure zero. Further partial results have been obtained for odd-periodic orbits and for algebraic boundaries. The full statement for arbitrary smooth strictly convex tables and arbitrary $n$ remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: No planar billiard possesses an open set of quadrilateral trajectories
status_evidence.snippet: For any domain with piecewise C^4-smooth boundary in the plane, the set of quadrilateral trajectories of the corresponding billiard has measure zero.
status_evidence.claim: Ivrii's conjecture is established for period 4 in the planar case.

status_evidence.title: Ivrii's conjecture for some cases in outer and symplectic billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Ivrii's conjecture (1980) states that the set of periodic billiard orbits in a domain with a smooth boundary has measure zero.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is widely cited as still open in general.

status_evidence.title: Examples of projective billiards with open sets of periodic orbits
status_evidence.snippet: In the class of projective billiards, counterexamples to Ivrii's conjecture have been exhibited.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture fails for the broader class of projective billiards, but the classical Birkhoff case remains open.
